method: Preheat the oven to 200°C, fan 180°C. Scrub the celeriac, leaving the skin on, then halve and finely slice into strips. Rub with the shawarma paste, a pinch of black pepper and 1 tbsp of red wine vinegar.
Thread the celeriac onto metal skewers, place on a baking tray and roast for 30 minutes, until sticky and caramelised, turning occasionally.
Coarsely grate or shred the red cabbage into a bowl, then toss with a small pinch of salt and 1 tbsp of red wine vinegar to make a quick pickle.
Tip the jalapeños, juice and all, into a blender and blitz with most of the coriander, stalks and all, until smooth. Pour back into the jar; it keeps in the fridge for a week.

For the flatbreads, put the flour in a large bowl with a good pinch of salt, then gradually whisk in 150ml of water and the olive oil. Knead for 1 minute into a smooth dough. Rest for a few minutes, then divide into 4 and roll out as thin as you can. Cook one at a time in a dry nonstick pan on a high heat for 1 minute each side, until golden and puffed up.
Spread the flatbreads with houmous and pile on the pickle. Slide the celeriac off the skewers and scatter over with the remaining coriander leaves. Drizzle over a little green sauce, to taste.
